name: Pyrénées - Mont Perdu
blurb: Izard, marmots and vultures on shared France-Spain summer pastures.

tip.title: Leave no flock on the pastures
tip.text: Livestock carcasses feed griffon and bearded vultures. Set Domestic sheep to -100% and see how the vultures and bear that rely on them fare.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Ordesa y Monte Perdido National Park

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Summer sunlight
nodes.desc: Short, bright high-mountain summers power the meadows and shrub heaths above the treeline.

nodes.name: Winter snowpack
nodes.desc: Deep snow covers the high ground for months and, as it melts, feeds the streams and lakes below.

nodes.name: Clear fast streams
nodes.desc: Cold, oxygen-rich mountain streams with permanent flow are the home of aquatic insect larvae and of the desman.

nodes.name: Seasonal grazing (transhumance)
nodes.desc: Flocks and herds are driven to high summer pastures each year, a long-running practice that helps keep the uplands open.

nodes.name: Soil fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down carcasses, dung, leaf litter and dead plants, returning nutrients to mountain soils.

nodes.name: Heather
nodes.desc: A low evergreen shrub of mountain heaths, eaten by deer and chamois.

nodes.name: Bilberry
nodes.desc: A berry-bearing dwarf shrub of sub-alpine slopes, browsed by deer and its fruit eaten by bears.

nodes.name: Mat-grass pasture
nodes.desc: A tough tussock grass that makes up much of the upland summer pasture grazed by flocks and wild herbivores.

nodes.name: European beech
nodes.desc: A main tree of the humid northern valley forests, giving leaves, buds and cover to deer and stream life.

nodes.name: Pyrenean chamois (izard)
nodes.desc: A sure-footed mountain goat-antelope that browses grass, lichens and buds on steep slopes up to about 3,000 m. It is the best-recorded large animal here.

nodes.name: Roe deer
nodes.desc: A small woodland deer that browses heather, beech and bilberry in the valley forests.

nodes.name: Alpine marmot
nodes.desc: Hibernating burrow-dweller of the high meadows, reintroduced to the Pyrenees in 1948. It eats grasses and herbs and whistles to warn of danger.

nodes.name: Domestic sheep
nodes.desc: The main livestock of the summer pastures. Dead animals left on the mountain feed vultures and other scavengers.

nodes.name: Caddisfly larvae
nodes.desc: Aquatic insect larvae in cold streams and the favoured prey of the Pyrenean desman.

nodes.name: Pyrenean desman
nodes.desc: A small, rare aquatic mole that eats mostly stream insect larvae, especially caddisflies. Its main predator is the otter.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Opportunistic hunter with many recorded prey here, including marmots and small mammals.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: A slim weasel relative that hunts marmots, hares and small animals even on high ground.

nodes.name: Griffon vulture
nodes.desc: A large cliff-nesting scavenger that feeds on carrion. It is the most-recorded bird of the area.

nodes.name: Bearded vulture
nodes.desc: Lives mostly on bones, dropping them from the air to crack open the marrow. Conservation plans target it at this World Heritage site.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: A cliff-nesting raptor of mountain regions that takes marmots, hares and other prey, and also feeds on carrion.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that gets most energy from plants and berries but also eats insects, carrion and young hoofed animals. Only a small population survives in the Pyrenees.

nodes.name: Eurasian otter
nodes.desc: A river hunter and the main predator of the Pyrenean desman.
